documents.title: Farmers turn to drones, with mixed results
documents.text:
On a windy morning outside the village of Alcott, agronomist Beth Carrow launches a small drone over a field of winter wheat. Within twenty minutes, the machine has photographed every row, and software has flagged three patches where the crop is thin and likely to be suffering from disease. Ten years ago, finding the same patches would have required a day's walk across the field.

Surveys suggest that about one farm in five in the region now uses drones for tasks that range from crop monitoring to spraying. Supporters point to savings on fertilizer and pesticide, which can be applied only where needed. One grower, Joaquin Ferreira, says that he has reduced his chemical costs by nearly fifteen percent. Yet he adds that the equipment has demanded far more time than he expected: "The machine is quick, but learning to interpret what it tells you is not."

Skeptics highlight the limits. Regulations restrict flights near roads and villages, and the drones cannot operate in rain or strong wind, which are common in the region during spring, when decisions matter most. Rural advisor Nadia Petrov warns small farms against buying equipment individually. "A drone costs the same as a good tractor attachment, and it sits unused for most of the year," she says. She encourages farmers to share machines through cooperatives or to hire operators for specific tasks.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the article?
choices: Farmers refuse to adopt any kind of modern technology
Drones help farmers but come with real limits
Regulations have banned drones in all rural areas
A village has replaced its tractors with new machines
questions.explanation: The article presents advantages (savings, speed) and drawbacks (learning time, weather, regulation).

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Ferreira say about his drone?
choices: It has failed to reduce his spending on chemicals
It cannot be flown over a large field of wheat
It is too noisy to be used near farm animals
Making sense of its data takes time to learn
questions.explanation: He says the machine is quick but learning to interpret what it tells you is not.

questions.prompt: Why is spring a difficult season for drone use?
choices: The weather often prevents flights
Roads are closed to farm vehicles
Crops cannot be photographed when green
Pesticides are not allowed in April
questions.explanation: Drones cannot operate in rain or strong wind, common in spring when decisions matter.

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Petrov recommend?
choices: Buying a tractor attachment instead
Waiting for regulations to change
Sharing the equipment with other farmers
Hiring more workers to walk the fields
questions.explanation: She encourages farmers to share machines through cooperatives or hire operators.

documents.title: Important information for Parkview Hospital visitors
documents.text:
Effective Monday 1 September, new visiting arrangements will apply at Parkview Hospital. Visiting hours on general wards will be 2:00 to 8:00 p.m. every day, instead of the current 10:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. The change has been introduced to allow patients to rest in the morning, when doctors' rounds and treatments take place. Visitors to the maternity ward and the pediatric unit may continue to visit between 9:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., and parents may stay overnight with their children.

No more than two visitors per patient are allowed at one time, and children under twelve may visit only with the permission of the ward manager. All visitors must clean their hands on entering and leaving each ward; hand-sanitizing stations are located at every entrance. Anyone with cold or flu symptoms, or who has had diarrhea or vomiting within the past 48 hours, is asked not to visit.

Patients nearing the end of their lives, or those who require particular support, may receive visitors at other times; relatives should speak to the nurse in charge. Visitor parking is available in the east car park at a rate of 4 dollars for up to four hours, and is free for family members of patients in intensive care.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the notice?
choices: To explain how to apply for a job at the hospital
To advertise services in the maternity ward
To announce new rules for people visiting patients
To ask the public to donate to the hospital
questions.explanation: It describes new visiting hours and conditions from 1 September.

questions.prompt: Why have the general ward hours been shortened?
choices: To let patients rest while treatment is given
To reduce the number of nurses who are needed
To free up beds for new patients overnight
To prevent the spread of flu during the winter
questions.explanation: Mornings are reserved for rest, doctors' rounds and treatments.

questions.prompt: Who may visit before 2:00 p.m.?
choices: A friend of a patient staying in a general ward
A child under twelve with a grandparent
A person who has the first symptoms of flu
A parent coming to see a child in the pediatric unit
questions.explanation: Pediatric and maternity visitors can attend from 9:00 a.m.

questions.prompt: What is NOT stated in the notice?
choices: Hands must be cleaned at the entrance
Families must book visiting slots in advance
Parking costs less for relatives in intensive care
Special arrangements exist for dying patients
questions.explanation: No booking is required; the other points appear in the text.

documents.title: Proposal to replace the customer database
documents.text:
To: Executive Committee
From: Arjun Mehta, IT Director
Subject: Recommendation on the replacement of the customer database

Dear members of the Committee,

As you know, our current customer database, installed in 2012, has become a source of recurring problems. The vendor will stop providing security updates at the end of next year, and our teams report that searches can take up to a minute during busy periods. I have spent the last two months evaluating the alternatives, and I recommend that we replace the system with the cloud-based product offered by Stratus CRM.

The main advantages are lower maintenance costs and the ability to use the system from any location. Stratus would cost 94,000 dollars in the first year, including data migration and staff training, then 60,000 dollars annually, compared with 85,000 dollars a year for the present arrangement. The break-even point would therefore be reached in the fourth year. [A] There are, however, risks. Data would be stored outside our premises, and some clients in the public sector require that their records remain in the country. [B] Stratus has confirmed that it can offer storage in a national data center for an additional fee of 6,000 dollars per year.

Should the Committee agree, the migration would take about four months and would be scheduled for the quiet period beginning in January. [C] I would welcome the opportunity to present the details at your next meeting. [D]

Regards,
Arjun Mehta

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To report a security problem in the company
To recommend that a computer system be changed
To ask for a larger staff in the IT department
To describe a failed project in detail
questions.explanation: Mr. Mehta recommends replacing the customer database with Stratus CRM.

questions.prompt: What is a reason given for the change?
choices: The current system is too expensive for the company
Customers have asked for a mobile application
Employees have refused to use the old database
The supplier will stop issuing security updates
questions.explanation: Security updates stop at the end of next year; searches are also slow.

questions.prompt: What is the cost of the first year with Stratus, including the storage in the national center?
choices: 100,000 dollars
60,000 dollars
66,000 dollars
94,000 dollars
questions.explanation: The first year costs 94,000, plus the additional 6,000 for national storage, giving 100,000 dollars.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "This difference would then continue to add up in the company's favor each year."
questions.explanation: The sentence continues the cost comparison and the break-even point mentioned just before [A], describing the savings after that point.

documents.title: Online chat: Conference registration
documents.text:
Delegate (Priya Chandran): Hello, I registered for the Marlin Tech Conference but I haven't received a confirmation e-mail. I paid last Monday.
Support (Greg): Hello Ms. Chandran. Could you give me the e-mail address you used and the amount you were charged?
Delegate: priya.chandran@orbitworks.example, 495 dollars.
Support (Greg): Thanks. I can see a payment of 495 dollars, but the registration status is "pending." It sometimes happens when the billing address doesn't match the card issuer's records. Did you use a corporate card?
Delegate: Yes, it's my company's card, and the billing address is our head office in Rotterdam, but I entered my home address.
Support (Greg): That explains it. I can correct the address for you, but I need written confirmation from the card holder. Could you forward a message from your finance department?
Delegate: I can ask them today. Will the early-bird rate still apply? It ended on Friday.
Support (Greg): Because you paid before the deadline, you'll keep that rate. I'll make a note of that on your account so it isn't changed. Once I have the confirmation, the e-mail will be sent within an hour.

questions.prompt: What problem does Ms. Chandran report?
choices: Her card was charged twice for the same event
The conference has been moved to a later date
No proof of her registration has reached her
She is unable to log in to her online account
questions.explanation: No confirmation e-mail arrived after payment.

questions.prompt: What caused the problem?
choices: The company card she used had already expired
The deadline for the early-bird rate had passed
The address she gave differs from the bank's records
Her e-mail address had been spelled incorrectly
questions.explanation: Greg says it happens when the billing address doesn't match the issuer's records; she entered her home address.

questions.prompt: What does Greg need from her?
choices: Written approval from the finance team at work
A copy of the receipt for the payment she made
A photograph of the corporate card she used
The address of her home that she entered earlier
questions.explanation: He needs confirmation from the card holder, which means her finance department.

questions.prompt: What will happen to the price she paid?
choices: It will increase by 10 percent
It will be refunded after confirmation
It will be reduced for the next event
It will not be altered despite the delay
questions.explanation: She paid before the deadline, so she keeps the early-bird rate and a note is added to her account.

documents.title: Research Coordinator, Halvorsen Foundation
documents.text:
The Halvorsen Foundation, an independent funder of environmental research, seeks a Research Coordinator to manage its portfolio of twenty grants. You will review progress reports, organize annual review meetings, and advise grant holders on reporting requirements. The post involves up to ten days of travel per year, mostly within Europe.

Candidates should hold a master's degree in a natural science and have at least two years of experience in research administration or project management. Excellent writing skills are essential, as you will draft summaries for the board. Knowledge of Norwegian is a plus. We offer 48,000 to 55,000 euros, 28 days of leave and a pension plan. The post is based in Bergen, with the possibility of working from home for one day per week. Applications should be sent by 15 March; interviews will take place on 4 and 5 April.

documents.title: Application: Research Coordinator
documents.text:
Dear Selection Committee,

I am writing to apply for the post of Research Coordinator. I hold a master's degree in marine biology, and for the past three years I have been the project manager of a European research network involving eleven universities. In this role I prepare the annual reports sent to the funder and organize two meetings per year for around eighty scientists. I do not speak Norwegian but have been learning it for six months.

I am interested in the Foundation's work on coastal ecosystems, which is close to my own field. My only reservation concerns relocation: my partner works in Oslo, and I would hope to work from home on two days instead of one. Would this be possible?

Yours faithfully,
Ingrid Solheim

documents.title: Re: Application: Research Coordinator
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Solheim,

Thank you for your application. The committee was impressed by your experience and would like to interview you on 5 April at 2 p.m. Please prepare a short presentation on how you would handle a grant holder who repeatedly submits reports late.

On working arrangements, the Foundation is willing to consider two days at home after your probation period of six months, though attendance in Bergen would be required during the annual review meetings. We would also be glad to fund Norwegian lessons.

Please confirm by 20 March.

Best wishes,
Thomas Aune, Operations Director

questions.prompt: Which of the Foundation's requirements does Ms. Solheim clearly meet?
choices: Knowledge of the Norwegian language at a high level
A science degree and experience in managing projects
Previous experience of working as a grant holder
A background in giving advice to a board of directors
questions.explanation: She holds a master's in marine biology and manages a research network; Norwegian is only a plus and she is still learning it.

questions.prompt: What is Ms. Solheim's concern?
choices: Whether the pay is high enough for her family
How many days of work she could do at home
How often she would have to travel for the job
Whether the post requires her to speak Norwegian
questions.explanation: She would hope to work from home two days instead of one, because her partner works in Oslo.

questions.prompt: How does Mr. Aune respond to her request?
choices: He rejects it completely
He accepts it from the first day
He postpones the decision to April
He accepts it, with conditions
questions.explanation: Two days at home are possible after the six-month probation period, with attendance at annual meetings.

questions.prompt: What does the invitation suggest about the interview?
choices: Candidates will have to show good practical judgment
It will include a test of Norwegian language skills
It will take place by video call from Oslo
It will bring several candidates together in a group
questions.explanation: She is asked to prepare a presentation on handling a grant holder who submits late reports.

questions.prompt: When must Ms. Solheim reply?
choices: By 15 March
By 4 April
By 20 March
By 5 April
questions.explanation: Mr. Aune asks for confirmation by 20 March; 15 March was the application deadline and 5 April is the interview date.

documents.text:

Items must be ready for collection at the venue by 11 a.m. on the day after the event. Payment is due within 14 days. Damage to equipment will be charged at replacement cost.

documents.title: Question about the invoice
documents.text:
Dear Meridian,

Thank you for the equipment, which arrived on time and was in good condition. When we reviewed the invoice, we noted that the sound system charge of 450 dollars was not in the original quote of 20 May, which listed only the stage and lighting package. Our event coordinator says that the technician stayed only for the first two hours of the dinner. Also, we were told that the discount would apply to all hire items; I am not sure that the amount shown reflects this.

Could you review and send a corrected invoice?

Sincerely,
Mona Kessler

documents.title: Re: Question about the invoice
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Kessler,

I have checked our records. The sound system was added on 2 June at the request of your coordinator, and I attach her message. The technician's fee is fixed and does not depend on the length of the stay. I accept, however, that the discount was calculated incorrectly: it should apply to all the hire items, but not to delivery, which is a service. I have recalculated it, and the corrected discount is 15 percent of 1,974.00 dollars.

A revised invoice is attached. The payment date remains the 24th.

Regards,
Jaime Torres, Accounts

The condition of the chairs and the tables received

questions.explanation: She says the 450-dollar sound system charge was not in the quote.
